title: How to become a billionaire
paragraphs: Have you ever fancied sailing around the world in your own yacht or buying a holiday home in the Caribbean? Well, before you get too excited, it may help to find out if you have what it takes to become a billionaire.

We've all heard stories of school drop-outs who have made their fortune, but are they the norm or an exception to the rule? Do they tend to be university graduates or self-made entrepreneurs? Are they married or single?

Thanks to a recent analysis of people in Forbes Top 100 Billionaires List, we can now find out what the world's mega rich have in common. We know which star sign is the most popular amongst multi-millionaires, what percentage wear glasses and even how many are bald!

If you are deciding whether or not to go to university, it may help you to know that 76% of the richest people in the world have a degree. According to this study, of those 76%, 47% have a bachelor's degree, 23% have a master's and 6% have a doctorate. Don't lose hope if you aren't very academic though. It's worth noting that many of those on the list did not pass all their exams with flying colours. Microsoft founder Bill Gates dropped out of Harvard University after two years of study. And Chinese business magnate Jack Ma, failed his university entrance exams three times before going on to complete his degree and make his millions.

Another interesting trend is that the world's high-fliers are much more likely to be married - only 12% of billionaires are unmarried. You are also more likely to make it if you were born under the most popular star sign, Aquarius, than if you are a Cancer - the least popular sign on the zodiac. Finally, the percentage of billionaires who are bald is quite high - so don't worry if you're losing your hair, you may get to sail that yacht around the Caribbean after all!

vocabulary.entry: fancy [v.] /ˈfænsi/ 幻想；想要 (英式英语；口语)
vocabulary.example: Do you fancy going to the cinema tonight?
vocabulary.translation: 你今晚想去看电影吗？

vocabulary.example: They spent their summer vacation on a luxury yacht.
vocabulary.translation: 他们在一艘豪华游艇上度过了暑假。

vocabulary.example: The Caribbean is a popular destination for cruise ships.
vocabulary.translation: 加勒比海地区是游轮的热门目的地。

vocabulary.example: He became a billionaire after selling his tech company.
vocabulary.translation: 出售他的科技公司后，他成了亿万富翁。

vocabulary.entry: school drop-out [n.] /skuːl ˈdrɒpaʊt/ 辍学者 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Some famous inventors were school drop-outs.
vocabulary.translation: 一些著名的发明家曾是辍学者。

vocabulary.example: He made a fortune in the oil business.
vocabulary.translation: 他在石油生意中发了财。

vocabulary.example: In this culture, eating rice with every meal is the norm.
vocabulary.translation: 在这种文化中，每餐吃米饭是常态。

vocabulary.entry: exception to the rule [phr.] /ɪkˈsepʃən tə ðə ruːl/ 例外情况 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Most of the students passed, but she was the exception to the rule.
vocabulary.translation: 大多数学生都通过了，但她是个例外。

vocabulary.example: He is a self-made millionaire who started with nothing.
vocabulary.translation: 他是一位白手起家的百万富翁，从一无所有开始。

vocabulary.example: The young entrepreneur started her first business at 18.
vocabulary.translation: 这位年轻企业家18岁就创办了她的第一家公司。

vocabulary.entry: mega rich [adj.] /ˈmeɡə rɪtʃ/ 超级富豪 (口语；前缀mega-表示“巨大的”)
vocabulary.example: The mega rich often own multiple homes around the world.
vocabulary.translation: 超级富豪通常在世界各地拥有多处房产。

vocabulary.entry: star sign [n.] /stɑː saɪn/ 星座 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: What's your star sign? I'm a Leo.
vocabulary.translation: 你是什么星座？我是狮子座。

vocabulary.example: He started going bald in his twenties.
vocabulary.translation: 他二十多岁时就开始秃头了。

vocabulary.example: She has a degree in economics from Cambridge.
vocabulary.translation: 她拥有剑桥大学的经济学学位。

vocabulary.entry: bachelor's degree [n.] /ˈbætʃələz dɪˈɡriː/ 学士学位
vocabulary.example: A bachelor's degree is often required for entry-level jobs.
vocabulary.translation: 入门级工作通常要求学士学位。

vocabulary.entry: master's [n.] /ˈmɑːstəz/ 硕士学位 (master's degree的简称)
vocabulary.example: He is studying for his master's in engineering.
vocabulary.translation: 他正在攻读工程学硕士学位。

vocabulary.example: She earned her doctorate in neuroscience.
vocabulary.translation: 她获得了神经科学博士学位。

vocabulary.example: The school has a strong academic reputation.
vocabulary.translation: 这所学校有着良好的学术声誉。

vocabulary.entry: with flying colours [phr.] /wɪð ˈflaɪɪŋ ˈkʌləz/ 以优异成绩 (固定搭配；英式拼写，美式: colors)
vocabulary.example: She passed the exam with flying colours.
vocabulary.translation: 她以优异成绩通过了考试。

vocabulary.example: The oil magnate donated millions to charity.
vocabulary.translation: 这位石油大亨向慈善机构捐赠了数百万。

vocabulary.entry: high-flier [n.] /ˌhaɪ ˈflaɪə/ 成功人士；有潜力的人 (英式拼写，美式: high-flyer)
vocabulary.example: She is a high-flier who was promoted to manager at 25.
vocabulary.translation: 她是一位成功人士，25岁就被提升为经理。

vocabulary.example: People born under Aquarius are said to be independent and creative.
vocabulary.translation: 水瓶座出生的人据说独立且富有创造力。

vocabulary.example: Cancer is a water sign known for being emotional and intuitive.
vocabulary.translation: 巨蟹座是水象星座，以情感丰富和直觉敏锐著称。

vocabulary.example: The zodiac is divided into twelve signs.
vocabulary.translation: 黄道十二宫分为十二个星座。
